anchorData:
ROAD: 8,000 m stretch of Thika Road, Nairobi, starting at the Roysambu stage and heading towards Ruiru. It has 21 designated crossing points (zebra crossings or footbridges) and therefore 20 GAPS. A gap is the distance in metres between two neighbouring designated crossing points. School gate is at the 4,000 m mark. OFFICER'S CLAIM: 'The average distance between crossing points is about 400 m, so the road is well served.' CHECK: 8,000 m / 20 gaps = 400 m, so the claim is arithmetically true.

GAPS IN ORDER ALONG THE ROAD (m) and PEDESTRIANS crossing at undesignated spots in that gap during one weekday morning count, 6:30-7:30 am, Tuesday: G1 200 m, 3 | G2 150, 2 | G3 250, 4 | G4 100, 1 | G5 300, 5 | G6 200, 3 | G7 100, 2 | G8 250, 4 | G9 700, 18 | G10 1000, 26 | G11 1100, 31 | G12 800, 22 | G13 1050, 28 | G14 600, 15 | G15 200, 4 | G16 150, 2 | G17 100, 1 | G18 250, 3 | G19 300, 5 | G20 200, 3.
Totals: gaps sum to 8,000 m. Pedestrians sum to 182. Gaps G1-G8 sum to 1,550 m (1,550 m mark). The long stretch G9-G14 runs from the 1,550 m mark to the 6,800 m mark and includes the school gate. Its six gaps sum to 5,250 m, which is 65.6% of the road, and it has 140 of the 182 pedestrians (77%). The other 14 gaps total 2,750 m and have 42 pedestrians. Near-miss log kept for the week by matatu drivers (Mzee Otieno and colleagues): 12 near-misses, 9 of them (75%) inside the long stretch G9-G14.

UNGROUPED FREQUENCY TABLE OF GAPS (m: frequency): 100:3, 150:2, 200:4, 250:3, 300:2, 600:1, 700:1, 800:1, 1000:1, 1050:1, 1100:1. Total frequency 20. Sorted list: 100,100,100,150,150,200,200,200,200,250,250,250,300,300,600,700,800,1000,1050,1100. Ungrouped results: mean 400 m, median 250 m (10th and 11th values are both 250), mode 200 m (appears 4 times), range 1,000 m (1,100 - 100), shortest gap 100 m, longest gap 1,100 m. 14 of the 20 gaps are 300 m or shorter. Only 6 gaps are longer than 300 m and all six are over 500 m.

UNGROUPED PEDESTRIAN COUNTS PER GAP (count: frequency): 1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 4:3, 5:2, 15:1, 18:1, 22:1, 26:1, 28:1, 31:1. Total 20 gaps. Total pedestrians 182. Mean 9.1 per gap, median 4, mode 3, range 30.

GROUPED GAP DATA, equal class width 200 m. Classes: 0 to <200, 200 to <400, 400 to <600, 600 to <800, 800 to <1000, 1000 to <1200. Frequencies: 5, 9, 0, 2, 1, 3. Total 20. Midpoints: 100, 300, 500, 700, 900, 1100. f x midpoint: 500, 2700, 0, 1400, 900, 3300. Sum is 8,800. Grouped mean = 8,800/20 = 440 m (an estimate; it differs from the true 400 m because of grouping). Cumulative frequencies: 5, 14, 14, 16, 17, 20. Modal class is 200 to <400. Median class is 200 to <400 (the n/2 = 10th value). Grouped median = 200 + ((10-5)/9) x 200 = 311 m to the nearest metre (311.1). It differs from the true median of 250 m because grouping assumes values are spread evenly within a class.

UNEQUAL CLASS WIDTH VERSION (Lesson 6): classes 0 to <200 (width 200, f=5), 200 to <400 (width 200, f=9), 400 to <1000 (width 600, f=3: gaps 600, 700, 800), 1000 to <1200 (width 200, f=3). Total 20. Frequency density = frequency / class width in units of 100 m: 2.5, 4.5, 0.5, 1.5 respectively. Check: 5/2=2.5, 9/2=4.5, 3/6=0.5, 3/2=1.5. The widest class has the lowest bar even though it holds 3 gaps.

FREQUENCY POLYGON (Lesson 7), Thika Road, equal classes: plot (midpoint, frequency) = (100,5), (300,9), (500,0), (700,2), (900,1), (1100,3). Close the polygon with (-100,0) and (1300,0).
COMPARISON ROAD: Mombasa Road stretch near Embakasi, 20 gaps, surveyed by another group. Same classes with frequencies 4, 8, 5, 2, 1, 0 (total 20). Mean f x midpoint = 400+2400+2500+1400+900+0 = 7,600, so grouped mean is 380 m. Modal class is 200 to <400. Its longest gap falls in 800 to <1000 and it has no gap of 1000 m or more. Its polygon is a single hump with a short right tail, while Thika Road has a second small rise at 1000 to <1200. Similar means (440 vs 380) but different spread.
characters: Ruaraka Hills Secondary School (fictional), on Thika Road, Nairobi: the Grade 10 class does the project. Teacher: Mwalimu Wanjiru, who guides the survey. Learner group leaders: Achieng (data collection, tallies), Kiprop (tables and calculations), Njeri (graphs). County Road Safety Officer, Ms Halima Abdi: made the 'about 400 m average' claim. She is not careless or dishonest; her mean of 400 m is correct but incomplete. Mzee Otieno: a matatu driver on the Thika Road route who says most near-misses happen in one stretch. His log of 12 near-misses (9 in the long stretch) supports the data. Mombasa Road group: a partner school's learners who supply the comparison grouped data. Audience for the final presentation: the school principal, the Parents Association, the area chief and a representative from the county roads office. Thika Road: the main road with all primary data. Mombasa Road (Embakasi stretch): comparison data only. Learners use tally sheets, tape measures or trundle wheels, calculators, and a spreadsheet on a school computer or phone for polygons. Every lesson may rely on: the 20-gap data set in anchorData, the long stretch G9-G14 including the school gate, and the officer being right about the mean.
outcome: The learners' data show the officer's mean of 400 m is correct, but it hides the shape of the data. Fourteen of the 20 gaps are 300 m or shorter (median 250 m, mode 200 m), while six gaps of 600 m to 1,100 m cluster in one 5,250 m stretch that includes the school gate. In that stretch 77% of undesignated crossers (140 of 182) and 9 of 12 near-misses occur. The mean was pulled up by a few very long gaps, so one average cannot show where pedestrians are at risk. Median, mode, grouped tables, histograms and polygons together reveal the danger. The class recommends extra crossing points (for example a zebra crossing or footbridge near the school gate and in the 1000 to <1200 gaps) and presents this to the school administration, parents and community leaders. They note that this is a one-morning sample and should be repeated.
conventions: Use 'gap' for distance between two neighbouring designated crossing points, always in metres (m). 'Undesignated crossing' means a pedestrian crossing the road away from a zebra crossing or footbridge. 'Long stretch' means gaps G9-G14 only. Use 'data' as plural. Ungrouped data: individual values; grouped data: values in classes. Write classes as '200 to <400' (lower boundary included, upper excluded), equal width 200 m unless stated. Midpoint = (lower + upper)/2. Mean = sum of (f x x) / sum of f for ungrouped, with x = midpoint for grouped; say 'estimate' for grouped mean. Median for ungrouped: middle value (mean of the 10th and 11th for n=20). Grouped median = L + ((n/2 - cf)/f) x w, where L is the lower boundary of the median class, cf the cumulative frequency before it, f its frequency, w its width. Mode: most frequent value; modal class: class with highest frequency (for equal widths). For unequal widths, the tallest bar is the highest FREQUENCY DENSITY, not the highest frequency. Frequency density = frequency / class width in units of 100 m. Histogram bars touch, area represents frequency and the horizontal axis is continuous. Frequency polygon plots (midpoint, frequency) joined by straight lines and closed at both ends on the axis. Always give the road, the unit and the 20-gap sample when quoting figures. Never change anchorData numbers. The three KICD key inquiry questions (What is statistics? How do we represent data? How do we use statistics in day-to-day life?) are tracked on the DQB. Round grouped answers to the nearest metre. Say 'the officer's claim is true but incomplete', never 'wrong'.

lessonMap.focus: Is the road really well served? Data and where it comes from
lessonMap.teaches: What data and statistics are, and the sources of data (surveys, observation, records), used to plan how to test the officer's claim
lessonMap.buildsOn: None; launches the phenomenon with the officer's claim, the school-gate observations and Mzee Otieno's remark; starts the DQB and initial model
lessonMap.usesData: Officer's claim (400 m average, 8,000 m, 21 crossing points), the near-miss log (12 near-misses) and a first look at the idea of undesignated crossings; no calculations

lessonMap.focus: Counting the road: tallies and frequency tables
lessonMap.teaches: Collecting data with tally marks and organising ungrouped data into a frequency distribution table
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 1: data sources and the plan to observe and measure gaps and count pedestrians
lessonMap.usesData: The 20 gaps, the pedestrian counts per gap, the ungrouped frequency tables for both and the totals (8,000 m; 182 pedestrians)

lessonMap.focus: Mean, mode and median: which one tells the truth?
lessonMap.teaches: Calculating mean, mode and median of ungrouped data and judging which best represents it
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: the ungrouped frequency tables as the input for calculation
lessonMap.usesData: Gap mean 400 m, median 250 m, mode 200 m, range 1,000 m; pedestrian mean 9.1, median 4, mode 3; the sorted lists

lessonMap.teaches: Choosing class width and boundaries, building a grouped frequency table and identifying the modal class
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 2: frequency tables; Lesson 3: the range of 1,000 m, which shows why grouping is needed
lessonMap.usesData: Grouped gap table with classes of width 200 m (frequencies 5, 9, 0, 2, 1, 3) and modal class 200 to <400

lessonMap.focus: Mean and median from grouped data
lessonMap.teaches: Estimating mean using class midpoints and median using cumulative frequency and the formula, then comparing with ungrouped results
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 3: ungrouped mean and median (400 m, 250 m); Lesson 4: the grouped table
lessonMap.usesData: Midpoints, f x midpoint sum 8,800, grouped mean 440 m, cumulative frequencies 5, 14, 14, 16, 17, 20, grouped median 311 m

lessonMap.teaches: Drawing histograms with equal widths, then with unequal widths using frequency density
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 4: the equal-width table; Lesson 5: sense of how grouping changes estimates
lessonMap.usesData: Equal-width frequencies (5, 9, 0, 2, 1, 3) and unequal-width classes 0 to <200, 200 to <400, 400 to <1000, 1000 to <1200 with densities 2.5, 4.5, 0.5, 1.5

lessonMap.teaches: Drawing frequency polygons by hand and with a spreadsheet, and comparing two data sets by their polygons
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lesson 4: classes and midpoints; Lesson 5: midpoints; Lesson 6: reading shape from graphs
lessonMap.usesData: Thika Road polygon points (100,5) to (1100,3) closed at -100 and 1300, and the Mombasa Road frequencies 4, 8, 5, 2, 1, 0 with mean 380 m

lessonMap.teaches: Interpreting graphs and measures together to make evidence-based recommendations and communicating them to the community (final model and DQB review)
lessonMap.buildsOn: Lessons 1-7: all measures, tables and graphs; the final explanation of the phenomenon
lessonMap.usesData: Whole anchorData: long stretch G9-G14 (5,250 m, 140 of 182 pedestrians, 9 of 12 near-misses), mean 400 m versus median 250 m, histogram and polygon shapes, Mombasa Road comparison
